partners.mechanism_chain: DMP1 (HGNC:2797) —DECREASES→ Hypophosphatemia (HP:0002147); DMP1 (HGNC:2797) —DISRUPTS→ Bone mineralization (GO:0001507); Bone mineralization (GO:0001507) —LEADS_TO→ Rickets (HP:0005734); ITGA2B (HGNC:5665) —DISRUPTS→ Platelet activation (GO:0007593); Platelet activation (GO:0007593) —LEADS_TO→ Bleeding disorder (HP:0001871); Bone mineralization (GO:0001507) —BINDS→ Platelet activation (GO:0007593). partners.mechanism_chain: DMP1 (HGNC:2859) —LEADS_TO→ Hypophosphatemia (HP:0002147); ITGA2B (HGNC:5666) —DISRUPTS→ Platelet Activation (REACT:72803); Platelet Activation (REACT:72803) —INCREASES→ Calcium Signaling (GO:0005509); Calcium Signaling (GO:0005509) —LEADS_TO→ Thrombocytopenia (HP:0001873). Loss-of-function mutations in DMP1 lead to hypophosphatemia. While DMP1's direct role in platelet function is unclear, ITGA2B, encoding integrin alpha-IIb, is crucial for platelet aggregation. In fetomaternal alloimmune thrombocytopenia, antibodies against ITGA2B (or its partner ITGB3) impair platelet function, disrupting platelet activation and subsequent calcium signaling, leading to thrombocytopenia. The overlap is proposed through the convergence on downstream platelet activation and calcium signaling pathways, which are essential for hemostasis and are affected in both disease contexts, albeit through different primary genetic origins.
